question.problem: Find the surface area of the part of the plane $x=\frac{y-z}{3}$ whose projection onto the $yz$-plane is bounded by the constraints $1\le y\le 4$ and $1\le z\le 3.$
question.worked_solution:
For a surface $S$ defined by $x=f(y,z)$ with $(y,z)\in D,$ the surface area of $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂x}{∂y})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂x}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

In this case, our surface is given by

$$
x=\frac{y-z}{3},\,(y,z)\in D,
$$

where 

$$
D={(y,z)\,:\,1\le y\le 4,\,1\le z\le 3},
$$

as shown in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14119930/assets/3f06a9c686a935cb6c561affbcd224045618d9cacaf94eb7c9eab8a9ca8da44c.png)

Now, since

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{y-z}{3})=\frac{1}{3}, \\ \frac{∂x}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{y-z}{3})=-\frac{1}{3},\end{aligned}
$$

the surface area is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}\,\text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{∂x}{∂y})}^{2}+{(\frac{∂x}{∂z})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+{(\frac{1}{3})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{3})}^{2}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{1+\frac{1}{9}+\frac{1}{9}}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\sqrt{\frac{11}{9}}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{3}{∬}_{D}\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{3}\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{3}\cdot (4-1)\cdot (3-1) \\  & =2\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$
